card pr-wf-paused  [decided]
Postponed means not now. Rejected means wrong
why: Both reopen reasons leave a card nobody is working on. Postponed keeps the content true and fans out a calm mark. Rejected says the content is wrong and fans out the red one.
subtree: 2 cards, 2 decided

The distinction that survives #pr-wf-scope. Out of scope is not a third state — but *not now* and *wrong* are two, and `reopen` already separates them.

| | `--reason postponed` | `--reason rejected` / `invalidated` |
|---|---|---|
| the content | still true | now wrong |
| the mark it fans out | `paused` — calm, keeps the status colour | `stale` — red |
| where it goes | every card downstream, at any distance. A paused card is never reviewed, so the mark cannot move hop by hop | the next hop only (#vi-prop) |
| a conflict | if a postponement and an invalidation reach one card, **stale wins**. A real invalidation is never allowed to look calm | |
| return | expected. `rederive` clears it when work resumes | only by deciding the opposite, which is a new decision |

## The test

**Would you build it unchanged if you had the time?** Postponed: yes. Rejected: no, it would come back different.

#pr-logic is the postponed case and it is exactly right — "logic in a program, Markdown holds prompts" is still the answer. Only the engine build is deferred, and the mark reached four hops down to #vi-oos-render.

## Neither one is a status

A werk status describes the **decision**, not the build. #tracker is `decided` with nine decided cards under it and nothing published yet. That is not a contradiction, and it is not postponed either, because no reopen fired. Same reason the mark is drawn on top of the status colour instead of replacing it (`web/app.js:1570`), and the reason #pr-wf-scope refused a fourth `Status`.

card pr-wf-naming  [decided]
Rename the derived mark from paused to postponed
why: The reopen reason is postponed and the mark it produces is paused. Two words for one state, and the map shows the word that was never typed.

`ReopenReason` is `'postponed' | 'invalidated' | 'rejected'` (`src/types.ts:12`). The mark it fans out is called `paused` everywhere else. You type `--reason postponed` and the map answers `PAUSED`.

One word per meaning. Rename the mark.

## Scope

| file | occurrences of `paused` |
|---|---|
| `src/fold.ts` | 26 — the `paused` set, `deriveStaleness`'s return, the `Rollup` counters |
| `web/app.js` | 36 — `G.paused`, `classOf`'s `is-paused`, `.ring.paused`, the hover titles |
| `src/cli.ts` | 14 — the `reopen` output and the `show` trace |
| `src/types.ts` | 11 — `Rollup.paused`, `openPaused`, `protoPaused`, `decidedPaused` |
| `web/style.css` | 9 |

Mechanical. No behaviour changes. `stale` keeps its name: `invalidated` and `rejected` both produce it, so no single reason word fits it, and `stale` is the honest description of the state rather than the act.

## The one argument for keeping two words

It was deliberate, not drift — see the comment at `src/fold.ts:217`. *Postponed* names the **act**, and only the origin was postponed. *Paused* names the **state** of a dependent four hops away that nobody touched. After the rename, #vi-oos-render will read "postponed", which is not something anyone did to it.

Accepted anyway: the trace already says where the mark came from and how far away it is — #vi-prop-bornstale built exactly that. The word does not have to carry it.

card pr-wf-paused  [decided]
Paused and rejected are separate reopen reasons
why: A reopened card has two possible reasons. Paused means the content is still true and the work waits. Rejected means the content is wrong. Each reason puts a different mark on the cards that depend on it: paused is grey and keeps the status colour, stale is red.

The card now has the new title, "Paused and rejected are separate reopen reasons". I reworded the why and the table in the body.

**"Fans out a calm mark" means this.** When a card is reopened, every card that depends on it gets a mark. The word "calm" means the mark is grey and does not turn the card red. The word "fans out" means the mark spreads to all dependent cards, at any distance.

**No other card defines the split.** This card is the only place. These cards touch it:
- #pr-wf-scope says out of scope is the same as postponed.
- #vi-prop defines the red `stale` spread.
- #pr-wf-naming renames the mark from `paused` to `postponed`.

**The reason flag is still `--reason postponed`.** The new title uses "paused" because you asked for it. It does not match the flag. #pr-wf-naming says one word should name one meaning, so these two cards disagree. One of them needs a change.
